pr_title: Fix OSSL_STORE 'file:' scheme implementation so it ignores objects in PEM files that the user isn't interested in
pr_body:
The gist of the filter is implemented in DECODER, the 'file:' scheme implementation and the PEM to DER decoder only pass extra data to feed the filter.

As a consequence of this change, it was discovered that we don't treat the structure name specified by the user correctly.  The intention was always that it should specify the *outermost* structure, as given by the decoders.  However, we used it to filter the *innermost* structure, and were arguably not even doing that quite right.
So, there are places where EncryptedPrivateKeyInfo need to be specified, rather than PrivateKeyInfo, and by consequence, there's a need for encoders with that output structure (or test_encoder_decoder fails).

See commits for details.

Fixes #16224
pr_comments: This is currently in draft, 'cause one of the tests is failing.

> Good work! This is much less invasive than I expected.

It's not going to stay that way, unfortunately...  we're not handling the user specified structure setting right, it's supposed to be the *outer* detectable structure, not somewhere further in.
For an encrypted PKCS#8 object, the outer structure is EncryptedPrivateKeyInfo, not PrivateKeyInfo.

I'm almost there, but I've hit some quirks where EOF is suddenly not detected even though the decoding process should have reached EOF...
I think I finally got it right.  Will push the changes in a moment, just running through the test suite once more
Should there be a test case for #16224?
Still does not look that much invasive.

> Should there be a test case for #16224?

Thanks for the reminder, I'm about to add one now.
This pull request is ready to merge

Merged

issue_context.title: `OSSL_STORE_load()` loading certs can be mislead to prompt for password
issue_context.body:
In case an (e.g., PEM formatted) certificate input file includes an encrypted key,
OSSL_STORE emits an unexpected and useless password prompt for it.

Here is a simple example, where the user needs to hit the Enter key for the `openssl verify` command to complete.
```
cat test/certs/root-cert.pem test/certs/key-pass-12345.pem >tmp.pem
apps/openssl verify -trusted tmp.pem test/certs/root-cert.pem
Enter pass phrase for tmp.pem:
test/certs/root-cert.pem: OK
```

Here is the stack trace for it:

comments: Apparently with the current codebase this will be quite hard to fix.
OTC: This should either be documented or fixed for 3.0 (if the scope of the fix is not fundamental)
@DDvO, would you mind grepping for `BEGIN` in that PEM file?  I want to see what PEM types are in there.
On the last OTC call, we concluded that this is a regression that's serious enough to do some digging.

> @DDvO, would you mind grepping for `BEGIN` in that PEM file? I want to see what PEM types are in there.

Simply see the example I gave in the OP:
```
cat test/certs/root-cert.pem test/certs/key-pass-12345.pem >tmp.pem
grep BEGIN tmp.pem
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
-----BEGIN ENCRYPTED PRIVATE KEY-----
```

> On the last OTC call, we concluded that this is a regression that's serious enough to do some digging.

This issue also indicates an inefficiency: If for instance just certs should be loaded from a file, there is no need to (deeply) parse other contents and (temporarily) build up internal representations for them.
With PEM input it should be straightforward to gloss over other contents, but maybe not for other types like PKCS12.
The PKCS12 support in store is making this problematic. Otherwise we would be able to avoid even setting the password prompt callback when we just want certs or crls.
A PKCS#12 file is a separate question...

Yes, I've mentioned it only because there might be workarounds/fixes that could be applied to fix this issue but would regress on the possibility to read the cert from a PKCS12 file which requires prompting for password.
Yup.  That's not a regression per se, though.
OTC: this is not a blocker for 3.0.  However, a fix for this will be included if available.

review_comments: Should this be CRL instead? Or `X509 CRL` to match with the PEM header for CRLs?

I've use the structure names from the ASN.1 modules.  That's why you see things like "SubjectPublicKeyInfo", "PrivateKeyInfo", "EncryptedPrivateKeyInfo", ...  "Certificate" and "CertificateList" follows that line of thought.
We did at some point think about using the PEM names as structure names, but never went through with it.  It would probably be quite disruptive at this point...
